clue.text: E.g. first row in examination

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means the first word is placed inside the second

blocks.note: an oral is a spoken examination
a row is a noisy commotion, a din

explanation.surface: A student sitting in the front row during an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: Row here is the noise, rhyming with cow, not a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Words like first, second and third are ordinal numbers, giving position in a sequence.

clue.text: Broadcast cut poor rock

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered widely, so these letters are strewn into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A news item about cutbacks that hit the poor hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' and 'cut' tempt a charade of OUT plus CROP, but the anagram uses both cut and poor.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcrop is a mass of bedrock that sticks out above the soil surface.

clue.text: Friend wandering after desperate deed without a navigational aid

indicators.note: wandering means straying from a fixed course, so the letters move around
after means coming later, so the jumbled friend is placed second, behind the deed phrase
without means lacking, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: dire means desperate, as in 'dire straits'
a deed is an action
the letter to remove
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lost friend wandering after a desperate act, with no way to navigate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Friend' opens the clue but its jumbled letters end the answer, because 'after' sends them behind the desperate deed.
explanation.definitionFit: A direction finder is a radio device that fixes the bearing of a signal, used by ships and aircraft to navigate.

clue.text: Fresh members of team bowled no differently

indicators.note: differently means in another way, so the letters are put in another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: New cricketers in the side bowled no differently from the old ones.
explanation.walkthrough: Bowled is cricket, which makes 'team' feel like the definition's sport.
explanation.definitionFit: New blood is an idiom for recent recruits who bring fresh energy to a group.

clue.text: Fill column

blocks.note: first meaning: to put a layer inside, as one does a coat or the stomach
second meaning: a file of people or things one behind another

explanation.walkthrough: Fill here is to cover the inside, as in lining one's pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for padding the inside of something and a noun for a row or queue.

clue.text: Longing to join network, about to make entrance

indicators.note: joining means attaching one thing to another, so the longing is tacked on after the network
turned about means facing the other way, so the network word is read backwards

blocks.note: a web is a network
an itch is a longing or craving

explanation.surface: Someone longing to join a social network so they can make a grand entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: Entrance is the verb (to enchant), stressed on the second syllable, not the doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is to cast a spell over them, a synonym for this verb.

clue.text: Late supporting round of applause

blocks.note: to be behind someone is to support them
'give them a hand' means applaud

explanation.surface: Applauding a performer, though rather late.
explanation.definitionFit: Behindhand means behind schedule or in arrears, a synonym for overdue.

clue.text: Cautious about alien, upset and weak

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns something on its head, so the alien is read upwards
about means around, so the cautious word wraps the other piece

blocks.note: wary means cautious
ET is the film alien, the Extra-Terrestrial

explanation.surface: A nervous person, wary of an alien, left shaken and feeble.
explanation.definitionFit: Watery tea or soup is thin and diluted, so it describes something lacking strength.

clue.text: True supporter prepared for north gets wet

indicators.note: prepared means made ready by working on it, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A loyal fan, ready for the trip north, gets soaked.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole tail of the clue, fifteen letters, is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A tower of strength is an idiom for someone who gives steadfast help and comfort in hard times.

clue.text: Leave area under cover in boat

indicators.note: in a down clue under means coming below, so the area letter follows the cover
in means placed inside, so these pieces go within the boat

blocks.note: a hoy is a small coastal sailing vessel
a lid is a cover
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Taking leave by sailing off under cover in a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: A hoy is an old small coasting boat, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Leave from work is time off, which is what a holiday is.

clue.text: Give up project with silly title when receiving nothing

indicators.note: receiving means taking something in, so the zero joins the other letters
silly suggests something muddled and senseless, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: to project is to throw
taken as written
taken as written
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone abandoning a project when it ends up with a silly title and gets nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram takes both title and when, plus the O they receive.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase comes from boxing, where a trainer concedes defeat by tossing a towel into the ring.

clue.text: Evoke scene of public games and everything

blocks.note: a rec is a recreation ground, a British public park for sport
all means everything

explanation.surface: Bringing to mind memories of the local playing field.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the rec is the local recreation ground where public games are played.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke a memory is to bring it back to mind, a synonym for this verb.

clue.text: Radiation during and following unusual day

blocks.note: in means during, as in 'in the night'
f. is the abbreviation for following
rare means unusual
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: Radiation recorded during, and after, a strange day.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the band of electromagnetic radiation just beyond visible red light, felt as heat.

clue.text: Restaurant's decline is followed by most of chain

indicators.note: most of means not the whole, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: rot is decay or decline
taken as written
a chain of events is a series

explanation.surface: A restaurant chain on the slide.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'is' in the clue is used as letters, not as a link; 'followed by' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotisserie is a restaurant specialising in meat roasted on a turning spit.

clue.text: System of belief in operation aboard holy ship at sea

indicators.note: something aboard a vessel is inside it, so one piece goes in among the other letters
at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: OP is the common short form of operation
taken as written

explanation.surface: A religious creed practised aboard a sacred vessel sailing the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in operation' reads like a phrase but supplies OP, which joins the letters of holy ship before the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A philosophy is a set of principles or beliefs by which someone lives.

clue.text: Uncertain moment with judge absent

indicators.note: absent means not there, so that letter is taken away

blocks.note: a jiffy is a moment
J is the abbreviation for judge

explanation.surface: An awkward moment of doubt when the judge fails to appear in court.
explanation.definitionFit: Iffy is informal for doubtful or dubious, so it is a synonym for this adjective.

clue.text: Carving giant warped painting up

indicators.note: warped means twisted out of shape, so the letters are bent into a new order
in a down clue up means read from the bottom, so the painting word goes backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
an oil is a painting in oil paints

explanation.surface: A huge carving and a distorted painting hung up.
explanation.definitionFit: Intaglio is a design incised into a surface, the opposite of relief carving.

clue.text: Reportedly pointless blade

indicators.note: reportedly means as people say it, so the sound counts, not the spelling

blocks.note: vain means pointless, to no purpose

explanation.surface: A knife described as having no point.
explanation.definitionFit: A vane is one of the flat blades of a windmill, turbine or propeller.

clue.text: View across middle of grounds with lake and river

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letter, the only one kept
lying across something means stretching over it, so the view word spans the others

blocks.note: a vista is a view
the fourth of its seven letters
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A view across the middle of the estate grounds to a lake and river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vistula is the longest river in Poland, flowing through Warsaw to the Baltic.

clue.text: Flower in good composition held by small child

indicators.note: something held by another is gripped inside it, so these pieces go within the child word

blocks.note: a mite is a small child
G is the abbreviation for good
a nonet is a musical composition for nine players

explanation.surface: A child clutching a flower in a well-composed scene.
explanation.walkthrough: Composition is musical: a NONET is a piece for nine instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: Mignonette is a fragrant garden plant with small greenish flowers, an example of the category.

clue.text: Land in trouble right after changing cue

indicators.note: changing something alters its form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
ado is fuss or trouble
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: An actor lands in trouble straight after altering a cue.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecuador is a country in South America on the equator, a land in the sense of a nation.

clue.text: Fearful bother between son and daughter

indicators.note: something between two things sits inside them, so it goes in the middle

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
to bother is to care, as in 'don't bother'
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A parent anxious about trouble brewing between their son and daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Scared and fearful are synonyms, both meaning frightened.

clue.text: Diamonds perhaps with justification in item of luggage

blocks.note: diamonds is one of the four suits in a pack of cards
a case is an argument or justification, as in 'make a case'

explanation.surface: A smuggler with diamonds stashed in a bag, perhaps with an excuse ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks diamonds as an example of a card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitcase is a rectangular case with a handle for carrying clothes when travelling.

clue.text: Good meal for all to see including a cake

indicators.note: including means taking something in, so that letter goes inside the other pieces

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
tea is an evening or afternoon meal in Britain
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fine meal laid out for everyone to see, with a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film rating meaning suitable for everyone; A slips in after the G.
explanation.definitionFit: A gateau is a rich layered cake, often filled with cream, a type of the thing named.

clue.text: Composer raised in US evidently

indicators.note: in means contained within, so the letters lie inside the following words
in a down clue raised means lifted upward, so the letters are read bottom to top

blocks.note: the letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A composer clearly brought up in America.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Ives was indeed an American composer, so the surface is true.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Ives was a modernist American composer, an example of the category named.

clue.text: Poor distracted prude driven to cover one limb

indicators.note: distracted means mentally all over the place, so the letters are scrambled
covering something means wrapping around it, so the jumble goes round the other pieces

blocks.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one
a leg is a limb

explanation.surface: A frazzled prude reduced to covering up a single exposed leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driven' looks like part of the story but is fodder alongside prude.
explanation.definitionFit: Underprivileged describes people lacking money and opportunity, so it means poor in the social sense.

clue.text: Raised band led by sailor in trim

indicators.note: being led by someone means following behind them, so the sailor goes in front

blocks.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
a ridge is a raised strip or band

explanation.surface: A band of musicians on a stage, fronted by a sailor in smart dress.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to shorten it, as one would trim it down.

clue.text: Put out from southern source

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
a mother is the origin or source of something, as in 'mother of invention'

explanation.surface: Information put out by a source in the south.
explanation.definitionFit: To smother a fire is to extinguish it by cutting off its air, one sense of the phrasal verb.
